title: F5: export-name mangling so zena can satisfy interface exports
description: component new requires mangled core export names (ns:pkg/iface@ver#func) for interface exports; zena export names are identifiers only. This blocks the two static-composition matrix cells (zena as generator under wac). Proposed: export-naming decorator (e.g. @exportName) on exported functions, mirroring @external on imports.
acceptance_criteria: zena component can implement rektide:interop/rng exports; interop-matrix static cells zena->rust and zena->zena flip to PASS; compiler suite green.
notes:
G agent launched 2026-09-15 on fork export-naming decorator; verify via interop-matrix static cells.
F5 landed. Fork: @exportName decorator (commit tsumxvov / 048e345c) renames the core-level export of export let/var and export declare function — parser carries @exportName("...") onto decl.exportName (codegen already had untyped hooks), checker diagnoses duplicate core export names, all four codegen export sites typed. Verified end to end: examples/interop-matrix zena generator now exports both flat next and the mangled rektide:interop/rng@0.1.0#next under new world rng-source-both (jcona commit uywqxwn/deb4753e... see repo). Matrix: 10 pass, 0 skip, 2 n/a, 0 fail — zena→rust static and zena→zena static flipped SKIP→PASS, jshost cells unchanged. Compiler suite: 2311 tests, 2297 pass, 0 fail (2285 baseline + 12 new @exportName tests). Open edges: @exportName on classes (codegen reads decl.exportName but parser never populates); interface exports with resources (mangled name covers only plain funcs — resource exports need [resource-new]/[dtor]/[method] exports, untested); component-level export of a resource-having interface is future work.
Correction to prior note: the jcona-side matrix wiring commit is uywpyxwn (git deb4753e), 'interop-matrix: close the static gap'. Resources probe: exporting an interface with a resource fails at component new with 'failed to find export of interface rektide:interop/rstream@0.1.0 function [constructor]generator' — resource exports are additional mangled FUNCTION exports ([constructor]/[method]/[dtor]/[resource-new]), so @exportName can spell each, but full support also needs resource handle-ABI (own/borrow i32 handles + canonical dtor registration) that zena does not model. Naming gap closed; resource machinery is separate future work.
close_reason: Done + verified 2026-09-15: fork @exportName decorator (tsumxvov, suite cached-passing, build fresh) + matrix generator update (uywpyxwn). Acceptance met: interop matrix 10 pass / 0 skip / 2 n-a / 0 fail — zena→rust static and zena→zena static cells now PASS (wac fuses zena GC components via the mangled interface export).

title: W7+F3: p3/JSPI frontier research and optional experiment
description: Why: decides fork strategy F3 (jco/JSPI as zena's first async host driver) and informs F2. Characterize: jco preview3-shim surface, sync guests against async p3 worlds, JSPI feature-detect status, what a zena async guest would need. Nothing in motion yet - this is the launch point.
acceptance_criteria: doc/research/p3-frontier.*.md with verified answers + a go/no-go recommendation for F3 with evidence.
notes:
Started local-source research into preview3-shim, p3 sync/async lowering, JSPI engine status, and the F3 sequencing decision; will record a bounded experiment if feasible.
Completed doc/research/p3-frontier.solmax.md. Bounded GO for F3: use jco/JSPI as zena's first async host driver, initially limited to sequential awaits over custom Promise host imports while keeping general WASI on p2. Verified stock jco 1.33.0 with an actual zena WasmGC guest using sync canonical ABI over async WIT: a GC reference survived a delayed host Promise and returned 41 in Node 26.6.0 and unflagged Chrome 150; Firefox 152 lacks JSPI. Also proved the native p3 async-lower/waitable/callback/task-return ABI with a hand-written zena guest in Node and Chrome. preview3-shim 0.6.0 is broad but experimental on Node, random-only in practice in the browser, and jco run currently omits its package symlink. Corrected prior assumptions: generated async/p3 output requires JSPI; SuspendError handling is normalization, not fallback; current Chrome flags in jco tests are redundant.
close_reason: Acceptance met: p3-frontier.solmax.md characterizes preview3-shim, sync guests in async p3 worlds, JSPI engine support and hard dependency, native callback ABI requirements, reproducible experiments, and a bounded GO recommendation for F3. Verified in Node 26.6.0, unflagged Chrome 150, and Firefox 152 (expected no-JSPI failure).
